title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The surrounding pages build a topological theory of conical and cylindrical neighbourhoods of closed subspaces. The goal is to 'unfold' (déployer) a stratified space into a space with boundary and corners. The previous page states an equivalence of categories. On one side are systems (X, Y, (X_i), T), with T a conical neighbourhood of a closed Y in X compatible with closed subspaces X_i. On the other side are systems (X*, Ẋ, (X_i*), Y, Ẋ→Y), where X* is the 'unfolded' space and Ẋ⊂X* a boundary subspace. One recovers X as the pushout X* ⊔_Ẋ Y, a mapping-cylinder-type gluing. Under this equivalence, strictness of T corresponds to Ẋ being a 'bord' compatible with the X_i*. Equisingularity of T along the X_i corresponds to Ẋ→Y together with the Ẋ_i being a simultaneous locally trivial fibration.

This page (numbered 5; the whole page is struck through with diagonal lines, i.e. an abandoned draft). It begins the multi-stratum version.

Setup:
- X is a topological space and I a finite (initially 'ordered') set.
- (X_i)_{i∈I} is a family of closed subsets: first 'increasing', then 'covering' (recouvrante), and called a 'stratification of type I'.
- Crossed-out alternatives show hesitation over the axioms: (a) the family is locally finite; (b) i≤j ⇒ X_i⊂X_j; and setting X_i* = X_i.

Auxiliary boundary. Since neighbourhoods are to be constructed inductively over strata, one needs in addition a boundary subspace Ẋ ⊂ X that is strictly compatible with the family X_i. The aim is to define a 'conification' of the stratification, compatible with Ẋ. This is a coherent system of conical neighbourhoods of all strata, i.e. control data in the sense of Thom–Mather, but purely topological and with boundary.

Cases:
- I empty: the conification is the empty structure.
- I = {i}, X_i = Y: by definition, a conification is a strict conical neighbourhood T of Y in X such that:
  - Ẋ is (strictly) compatible with T;
  - writing Ṫ for the boundary ('la partie bord') of T, the intersection T̈ := Ẋ∩Ṫ is a boundary subspace of Ṫ. This is a codimension-2 corner; more precisely Ẋ∩T is a conical neighbourhood of Ẏ := Ẋ∩Y in Ẋ, with boundary T̈;
  - Ṫ → Y is a fibration, 'in a sense to be made precise', presumably compatible with T̈ → Ẏ.

The point: once a boundary is present, unfolding one stratum creates corners. The structure must therefore be stable under restriction to the boundary, in the same way that iterated blow-up of a stratified space yields a manifold with (fibred) corners. The draft breaks off, and the next page passes to germs of conical and cylindrical neighbourhoods instead.
errors: The page is crossed out by Grothendieck and the definition is left incomplete: the fibration condition on Ṫ → Y is explicitly 'à préciser', and the general case |I| > 1 is never stated.

The phrase as transcribed, 'que Ṫ soit un sous-espace bord de Y', is mathematically odd, since Ṫ is not a subspace of Y. The intended statement is more likely that T̈ = Ẋ∩Ṫ is a boundary subspace of Ṫ, mapping to Ẏ = Ẋ∩Y; the image is ambiguous here.
The axioms on the family (X_i) wavered between versions: ordered/increasing, locally finite, covering. 'Type I' stratification is not fixed on this page.

ideas.what: Unfolding a stratum: conical neighbourhood data of Y in X are equivalent to a space X* with boundary Ẋ and a map Ẋ→Y, with X recovered as X*⊔_Ẋ Y
ideas.modern_name: Blow-up/resolution of stratified spaces into manifolds with boundary ('unzipping', mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (control data, mapping cylinder neighbourhoods); Melrose, Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza 2012 (resolution to manifolds with fibred corners); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 2017 (unzips); Quinn 1988 (homotopically stratified sets)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un Programme §5–6 sketches tame ('modérée') topology and the equivalence between stratified spaces and 'déployed' spaces with boundary; no details there

ideas.what: Conification compatible with an auxiliary boundary Ẋ, producing corners T̈ = Ẋ∩Ṫ, as needed for an induction over strata
ideas.modern_name: Control data / systems of tubular neighbourhoods on stratified spaces with boundary; manifolds with corners and iterated fibration structures

ideas.what: Equisingularity as simultaneous local triviality of Ẋ→Y together with the Ẋ_i (from the previous page)
ideas.modern_name: Locally cone-like / topologically locally trivial stratification (Whitney/Thom isotopy conclusion)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather, Siebenmann (locally conelike TOP stratified sets, 1972)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions equisingularity and tame structures only in general terms

missed.claim: An abandoned attempt to axiomatize an inductive 'conification' of a finite stratification of a space with boundary, explicitly tracking the corner T̈ = Ẋ∩Ṫ. This is a purely topological version of iterated resolution into spaces with corners. The later literature did this in smooth or conically-smooth settings (ALMP, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka) rather than in Grothendieck's axiomatic topological one.
missed.quote: Pour faire des constructions des voisinages on a besoin de plus d'un sous-espace bord Ẋ de X, strictement compatible avec la famille des Xᵢ. On veut définir la notion de conification (compatible avec Ẋ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. It documents that Grothendieck saw corners as forced by the induction, anticipating the 'manifolds with fibred corners' viewpoint. The idea itself is now standard and the draft is incomplete.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a crossed-out draft definition. Its content (unfolding strata into spaces with boundary and corners, compatible conical neighbourhoods) matches ideas Grothendieck sketched in the Esquisse and that were later developed independently (Mather, Siebenmann, Quinn, ALMP, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka). It is of historical interest but contains no result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'une famille croissante[?]' is more likely 'une famille recouvrante de parties fermées de X' (the word written above 'de parties' reads like 'recouvrante').
'un voisinage tubulaire[?] strict[?]' is more likely 'un voisinage cônique strict' (inserted above the line).

There is a defined symbol 'T̈' (double dot), with 'déf T̈' written above, apparently T̈ := Ẋ∩Ṫ. The garbled 'Ẋ∩T soit un sous-espace bord de Ṫ ... Ẋ∩T = Ẋ∩Y' should probably read 'T̈ soit un sous-espace bord de Ṫ ... T̈ ... = Ẋ∩Y =: Ẏ'.
'(compatible avec Ẋ)' is written as an insertion '(comp. avec Ẋ)' above 'conification'.
The whole page is struck through with three long diagonal lines, so the entire text is cancelled, not only the individually crossed lines.
